Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Lena / Tom — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can move to a validation window for Dedicated capacity: 

TL;DR (asks):
- Target SLOs you mentioned: 95th percentile generation latency <= 220 ms for short interactive requests (~<60 tokens), and p95 <= 700 ms for mid-length requests (~<512 tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: target steady-state of ~200 requests/sec with spikes to 450 req/sec; expected concurrent live streams ~80 sessions.
- Streaming: client requires token-by-token streaming for interactive features (low-latency token flush).

What Redwood will do next:
1) Provide a recommended Dedicated sizing / GPU mix and reserved throughput options (performance vs cost).
2) Share a validation plan + test harness (attached: redwood_dedicated_perf_plan.xlsx).
3) Run an initial internal benchmark against model family you indicated (70B quantized variant) and return expected p50/p95 numbers for short and mid-length sequences.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_perf_plan.xlsx, gpu_comparison_h100_a100.pdf

Please confirm:
- Final list of representative prompts/payload sizes and any special tokenization differences.
- Whether 95th percentile SLOs are strict production SLOs or initial targets for the validation run.
- Preferred validation dates (we proposed Dec 20-22).

Next steps: if you confirm prompts and dates we’ll provision a Reserved Dedicated cluster for the 3-day validation and share the test harness and scripts.

Thanks — I’ll loop internal infra/bench team once you confirm.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — sizing suggestions

Thanks for the recap, Marissa — adding a few sizing notes from infra/solutions side. High-level recommendations based on the workload targets you shared:

1) GPU selection (short summary):
- H100 (80GB / HBM): best for high-throughput, low-latency streaming. For large quantized transformer models (70B Q4 variants) we see ~2.5–3x throughput vs A100 for same latency window when optimized with our runtime.
- A100 (80GB): solid general-purpose option; lower cost than H100 in some clouds but lower sustained streaming concurrency for the same p95.
- A30/A10: cost-effective for inference but expect 40–60% lower concurrency for streaming workloads.

2) Reserved throughput sizing (two options):
- Performance-focused: 4x H100 (reserved pool) -> target reserved throughput ~400–600 req/s steady with headroom for spikes to ~1,200 req/s (depending on prompt length). This comfortably meets p95 <= 220ms for short requests based on our internal benchmarks.
- Cost-balanced: 6x A100 (reserved pool) -> target reserved throughput ~300–450 req/s steady, spikes to ~800 req/s; p95 expected in the 300–450ms range for short requests.

3) Concurrency & batching: plan for a mix of small continuous streams and batched inference for backend jobs. For interactive streaming with 80 concurrent streams we recommend enabling continuous KV cache warming and a 200ms batching window for background jobs.

We’ll provide a short matrix (attached gpu_comparison_h100_a100.pdf) with expected p50/p95 numbers across short / mid-length tokens from our internal runs. 

If Shopwell wants to prioritize latency, go H100. If cost density matters and 300–450ms p95 is acceptable for short requests, A100 can be a good compromise.

Aditya

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — bench notes + harness

Augmenting with concrete bench numbers and a test harness plan. I ran a set of internal microbenchmarks on our reference 70B quantized family (Q4) with our latest runtime. Summary below (single-run numbers, internal lab):

Short requests (<= 60 tokens):
- H100 x1 (opt): p50 ~40ms, p95 ~180–220ms (steady-state, streaming enabled)
- A100 x1 (opt): p50 ~65ms, p95 ~300–380ms

Mid requests (~512 tokens):
- H100 x1: p50 ~420ms, p95 ~680–800ms
- A100 x1: p50 ~680ms, p95 ~1,100ms+

Notes:
- Numbers above assume warmed KV cache and enabled continuous batching for background work. Cold-start first token latency will be higher.
- Streaming overhead: token-by-token flush adds ~6–12ms per token depending on network and client ACK behavior. We recommend line-buffered flush every 1–2 tokens for best UX.

Proposed validation harness:
- We’ll provide a reproducible script (python + k6 wrapper) that runs representative prompt sets you provide, measures p50/p95, and captures traces.
- Baseline run: 2 hours with synthetic steady-state to verify p95 targets, followed by spike run (20min) simulating 2–3x traffic bursts.
- Artifact: benchmark_logs_dec10.tar.gz (contains raw traces, configuration, and CSVs).

Suggested validation cluster for Dec 20–22: provision 4x H100 reserved (as Aditya suggested for performance), reserved throughput set to 800 req/s (headroom for spikes), concurrency limit 120 (allows for connection overhead), streaming enabled with 100ms max batching window for background jobs.

If Shopwell confirms prompt samples I’ll sanity-run the harness on a small subset next week to pre-warm caches.

—Dev
